column1: # Upstream files this fork is permitted to modify.
# One entry per line: the repo-relative path, a TAB, then the reason the
# fork must diverge in that file. A placeholder reason fails the check —
# regenerate writes the marker, a person replaces it with the real reason.
# Paths are relative to the sync point in fork-upstream-sync-point, so an
# upstream merge moves this list. Regenerate in the same commit.
# Deleting an upstream file is never allowlistable. See lat.md/fork.md.

column2: CI is fork-owned by the repo owner's explicit sanction: the job must build this tree's own CLI, run the fork's suite, and run the upstream guard, none of which upstream's workflow does.

Upstream pins lars20070/lat-check-action@v1, whose action.yaml hardcodes `npm install -g lat.md` with no override; upstream's index parser reads only `- [[name]]` entries and calls every fork index file incomplete.

Upstream's ran on every push to main and published the `lat.md` package, which this fork does not own. Replaced wholesale by a tag-triggered job that refuses to run unless the package name is @plebeiantech/lat.md.
Upstream's agent instruction file. The fork appends a pointer to lat.md/fork.md so an agent reading it learns the fork's rules; the edit is a link, not a rewrite.
Byte-identical twin of AGENTS.md upstream, and kept identical here for the same reason.
Install and usage text names the scoped package and the fork's release assets. Upstream's README cannot describe a package it does not publish.
Documents Ruby in supported source analysis languages.
Upstream's CLI reference. Fork-added subcommands and flags have to be documented where a reader looks them up, and `lat check` validates the wiki links into them.
Upstream's development process doc, extended with the fork's own testing and CI conventions and linked to lat.md/fork.md.
Documents .rake and .rb support in external default-file-extension.
Root index of the knowledge graph. `lat check` fails unless every fork-owned document under lat.md/ is listed here, so a fork-owned doc forces an entry.
Upstream's markdown-conventions doc. The fork's index-entry link scheme is a markdown convention and belongs in it rather than in a second competing document.
Test spec for upstream's index check, extended where the fork extended the check. `require-code-mention` fails unless each new spec section sits beside its test.
Test spec for Ruby and Rake source symbol resolution; require-code-mention fails unless the spec section sits beside its test.
Test spec for the hook suite the fork extended, for the same require-code-mention reason.
Test spec for `lat init`, extended where the fork extended the command.
The tests index. Every fork-owned test spec file must be listed here or `lat check` fails.
Test spec for safe source syntax highlighting including Ruby and Rake.

The only place `name`, `version`, `repository.url`, and `homepage` live, and all four must differ for the fork to publish at all. Also carries the vendoring of `@lat.md/server`, which upstream depends on but has not published: it moves to devDependencies, `express` moves up, and `build` gains the vendor step.
